idea-plugin.name: Interface Sink Divergence Companion
idea-plugin.description:
Flags a call through an interface-typed reference, passing tainted HTTP input, where SOME real implementations log that input unsanitized (CWE-117/CWE-532) while at least one other real implementation never does -- the interface type alone never guarantees which behavior you get once dependency injection swaps implementations.

Combines TWO techniques this catalog already proved separately: the real Class Hierarchy Analysis from Interface Exception Divergence Companion (resolve EVERY concrete implementation, never discard for "ambiguity") with the taint-to-sink pattern from Log Injection Companion/the SpEL/ XPath/LDAP sink finders -- run INSIDE each real implementation's own body, not just at the call site.

Stated honestly: v0.1 only interfaces with 2-10 real implementations; taint only through a bare reference or one-hop concatenation, both at the call site and inside each implementation. No dedicated Marketplace plugin found for this exact angle.

Free. No license nags, no telemetry, no network calls.

localInspection.displayName: Interface implementations diverge on logging tainted input
